children: Shristi Achar Bengaluru: Seven of India's top nine outsourcing companies either sequentially increased or maintained operating margins in the second quarter, as efficiencies tied to AI helped partially offset revenue deflation attributed to the technology amid persistent macroeconomic uncertainty on either side of the Atlantic seaboard.

HCLTech's margin rose 131 basis points quarter-on-quarter to 18.2%, Tech Mahindra's increased 40 basis points to 14.8%, Wipro's climbed 50 basis points to 16.5%, LTM's edged up 10 basis points to 15.6%, and LTTS' expanded 60 basis points to 16.3%. One basis point is a hundredth of a percentage point.TCS margins held steady at 24%, while Coforge maintained 16%.

Infosys' margin was largely unchanged at 21% compared with 21.1%, and Persistent's profitability contracted 100 basis points to 15%. An analysis by Bengaluru-based tech consultancy UnearthInsight shows selling, general and administrative (SG&A) expenses fell sequentially relative to revenue at six of nine IT services companies in Q2 FY27.

Tech Mahindra's ratio declined to 12.8% from 14.1%, HCLTech's to 11.5% from 12.2%, Persistent's to 15.2% from 16.5%, Coforge's to 13.5% from 13.9%, Infosys' to about 10.1% from 10.4%, and Wipro's to 12.7% from 12.8%.

title: AI Efficiencies Shield Q2 IT Margins from Transatlantic Macro Headwinds
